text: it actually needs to be a group effort. It's a team sport.
speaker: April Dunford
context: Lenny asks about who should care about positioning beyond just founders. April explains that weak positioning often comes from misalignment across different departments - where founders, marketing, sales, and product teams all have slightly different understandings of the company's positioning. She emphasizes that positioning cannot be developed in isolation by one department and then imposed on others.
text_ko: 사실 이건 혼자서 할 수 있는 일이 아니에요. 팀 전체의 노력이 필요하고, 말 그대로 팀 스포츠예요.
text_zh: 这其实需要大家一起努力。这是个团队活儿。
text_es: En realidad tiene que ser un esfuerzo de todos. Es un trabajo de equipo.
key_sentence: Fixing this requires a group effort; it's a team sport.
original_text: So in the work I do, and even back when I was a VP marketing, if we're going to fix this thing, we can't just have the marketing department or just the product managers sit down and cook up new positioning and then heave it over the wall to everybody else, it actually needs to be a group effort. It's a team sport.

vocabulary.definition: A collaborative endeavor where multiple individuals contribute their skills and resources to achieve a common goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, a group effort is often necessary for project completion, fostering teamwork and shared responsibility among team members.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of collaboration and collective input, making it suitable for discussions about teamwork but less so for individual achievements.

vocabulary.definition: A type of activity or endeavor that requires cooperation and collaboration among members to succeed.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, describing a project as a team sport highlights the necessity of teamwork and interdependence among employees to achieve organizational objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used in a positive light to promote teamwork, it may imply that individual contributions are secondary to the group's success.

text: When it's working really well, it feels like magic and really great positioning feels obvious. You pitch it to people and they're like, 'Well, of course that's it.
speaker: April Dunford
context: Lenny asks what it looks like when you've nailed positioning and are in a good place with it. April explains that excellent positioning should feel natural and self-evident to customers. She uses Postman as an example - they have an API platform for building and using APIs, which sounds simple and obvious now, but wasn't always described that clearly.
text_ko: 정말 잘될 때는 마치 마법 같아요. 훌륭한 포지셔닝(positioning)은 너무도 당연해 보이고, 사람들한테 설명하면 '아, 당연히 그거네' 하고들 반응해요.
text_zh: 当定位策略真正奏效的时候，感觉就像变魔术一样神奇，好的定位让人觉得理所当然。你跟别人一说，他们马上就会想，"对啊，就应该是这样。"
text_es: Cuando funciona de maravilla, se siente como magia y un buen posicionamiento se ve súper obvio. Se lo presentas a la gente y te dicen: "Ah, claro, por supuesto que es eso."
key_sentence: Great positioning feels obvious and magical.
original_text: When it's working really well, it feels like magic and really great positioning feels obvious. You pitch it to people and they're like, 'Well, of course that's it. What else could it be?' One of my favorite companies, this is a company I worked with a little bit a couple of years ago is Postman.

vocabulary.definition: The strategic process of establishing a brand or product in the minds of consumers relative to competitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, effective positioning helps differentiate a product in the market, making it more appealing to a target audience and enhancing its perceived value.
vocabulary.nuance: Positioning can imply a deep understanding of market dynamics and consumer psychology, and should be used when discussing strategic marketing efforts.

vocabulary.definition: Easily perceived or understood; clear, self-evident.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, stating something is obvious can sometimes undermine the complexity of a situation or the insights of others.
vocabulary.nuance: Use with caution, as it may come across as condescending or dismissive of others' perspectives.

text: But particularly, I've worked a lot with companies doing deep AI stuff, deep, deep digital analytics and deep data stuff and you can't tell from looking at the website, whether it's working or not.
speaker: April Dunford
context: Lenny asks for examples of good positioning statements and well-positioned companies. April explains that B2B tech positioning cannot be judged by external observers - what matters is whether it resonates with the actual target buyers. She points out that deeply technical products may seem unclear to outsiders but should be crystal clear to qualified prospects.
text_ko: 특히 저는 딥 AI(deep AI) 쪽이나 정말 심층적인 디지털 애널리틱스(deep digital analytics)와 딥 데이터(deep data) 관련 작업을 많이 해봤어요. 그런데 웹사이트만 보면 그게 제대로 작동하는지 알 수가 없어요.
text_zh: 特别是，我跟很多做深度AI、深度数字分析和深度数据挖掘的公司合作过，你光看他们网站根本看不出来这些技术到底管不管用。
text_es: Pero sobre todo, he trabajado mucho with empresas que están metidas a fondo en IA, en analítica digital súper avanzada y en manejo de datos complejos, y no puedes saber si está funcionando o no solo viendo la página web.
key_sentence: you can't tell from looking at the website, whether it's working or not.
original_text: But particularly, I've worked a lot with companies doing deep AI stuff, deep, deep digital analytics and deep data stuff and you can't tell from looking at the website, whether it's working or not. The true test of whether the positioning's working or not is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something? That's the real test of it.

vocabulary.definition: Analytics refers to the systematic computational analysis of data or statistics, often used to uncover patterns, correlations, and insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, analytics is crucial for decision-making, allowing companies to optimize strategies based on data-driven insights and improve performance metrics.
vocabulary.nuance: While analytics can imply a rigorous, data-centric approach, it is essential to distinguish between basic data analysis and advanced predictive analytics, which uses sophisticated algorithms.

text: So in B2B, we have two sets of competitors. We have status quo, which is whatever the company is doing to attempt to solve the problem right now, even if it's crappy and not great.
speaker: April Dunford
context: Lenny asks about the first step in positioning work. April explains her methodology starts with understanding competitive alternatives - what you need to beat to win deals. She clarifies that B2B companies face two types of competition: the current status quo (existing solutions, even poor ones) and other vendors that make it onto the customer's shortlist when they decide to buy something new.
text_ko: 그래서 기업 간 거래(B2B)에서는 경쟁 상대가 두 갈래예요. 하나는 회사가 지금 문제를 해결하려고 시도하는 모든 방식, 즉 현상 유지(status quo)인데, 설령 부실하거나 만족스럽지 못하더라도 그게 바로 경쟁이에요.
text_zh: 在B2B领域，我们面临两类竞争对手。一类是现状竞争，就是客户公司现在用来解决问题的办法，哪怕这个办法很糟糕、效果不好。
text_es: Entonces en B2B tenemos dos tipos de competencia. Está el status quo, que es lo que sea que esté haciendo la empresa ahora mismo para intentar resolver el problema, aunque sea una porquería y no funcione bien.
key_sentence: We have status quo, which is whatever the company is doing to attempt to solve the problem right now.
original_text: So in B2B, we have two sets of competitors. We have status quo, which is whatever the company is doing to attempt to solve the problem right now, even if it's crappy and not great. And then there's if the company does decide they're going to buy something different, they usually make a short list, so it's whoever else lands on the short list.

vocabulary.definition: The existing state of affairs or the current situation within a particular context, especially in terms of business practices or market conditions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, referring to the status quo often serves to highlight the need for change or innovation, particularly when evaluating the effectiveness of current strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: Using 'status quo' can suggest a resistance to change or an acceptance of mediocrity, depending on the context in which it is applied.

text: Most folks will discount the status quo, but they shouldn't because in B2B we lose about 40% of our deals to quote-unquote, 'no decision,' which actually means we lost to the spreadsheet, we lost to pen and paper, we lost to interns.
speaker: April Dunford
context: April continues explaining competitive alternatives in positioning work. She emphasizes that companies often underestimate the status quo as competition, but this is a major mistake. In B2B sales, a significant portion of deals are lost not to competitors, but to customers deciding to stick with their current solution, no matter how inadequate it might seem.
text_ko: 대부분 사람들은 현상 유지(status quo)를 과소평가하곤 하는데, 그렇게 해선 안 돼요. B2B(기업 간 거래)에서는 거래의 약 40%가 소위 '결정 없음(no decision)'으로 날아가거든요. 그런데 그 '결정 없음'이라는 건 사실 스프레드시트(spreadsheet), 펜과 종이, 혹은 인턴에게 진다는 뜻이에요.
text_zh: 大多数人都不把现状当回事，但其实不应该这样，因为在B2B销售中，我们大概有40%的单子都败给了所谓的"不做决定"，说白了就是败给了Excel表格，败给了纸笔记录，败给了实习生在用的那些老办法。
text_es: La mayoría de la gente no le da importancia al status quo, pero es un error, porque en B2B perdemos como el 40% de nuestros deals por "no decision" - que en realidad significa que perdimos contra la hoja de cálculo, contra el papel y lápiz, contra los becarios.
key_sentence: Discounting the status quo leads to losing deals to no decision.
original_text: Most folks will discount the status quo, but they shouldn't because in B2B we lose about 40% of our deals to quote-unquote, 'no decision,' which actually means we lost to the spreadsheet, we lost to pen and paper, we lost to interns. And if we're not positioning well against that, we're never going to get the customer to come off of that.

vocabulary.definition: The existing state or condition of affairs, particularly in a social or organizational context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, maintaining the status quo can hinder innovation and adaptation, as companies may resist change in favor of familiar practices.
vocabulary.nuance: While sometimes seen as a safe option, clinging to the status quo can lead to stagnation and missed opportunities for growth.

text: And so we have to be able to give customers that when they get on the sales call with us.
speaker: April Dunford
context: April describes the B2B buying process where a decision-maker assigns someone (like John) to research and recommend a solution. She explains that this person needs to justify their choice to their boss and cannot just pick randomly. The best positioning helps customers understand how the market is segmented and why your solution is specifically right for their situation.
text_ko: 그래서 고객이 우리와 세일즈 콜(sales call)을 할 때 그걸 제공할 수 있어야 해요.
text_zh: 所以我们得确保客户跟我们销售沟通的时候，能得到这些东西。
text_es: Y por eso tenemos que lograr darle eso a los clientes cuando se suban a la llamada de ventas con nosotros.
key_sentence: give customers that when they get on the sales call with us.
original_text: And so we have to be able to give customers that when they get on the sales call with us. The best thing we could do is say, 'Look, buddy, there's lots of CRMs out there, and let me tell you how this market shakes out. These ones are really good for big enterprises. These ones are really good, if you got this. These ones are really good, if you got this. But look, if you're this, this and this, you really need these four things and we got that and that's why you should pick us.'

text: A better way I think is we know internally that it's the tuna fishing net. That's why we built it.
speaker: April Dunford
context: April discusses positioning strategy for early-stage companies. She uses a fishing net analogy to explain that while you may have built your product for a specific use case (tuna fishing), it's better to keep positioning somewhat loose initially rather than being overly restrictive. This allows the market to show you unexpected use cases and customer segments that might be even better fits.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 더 나은 방법은, 내부적으로 이건 참치잡이 그물(tuna fishing net)이라는 걸 알고 있다는 거예요. 그래서 그걸 만든 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得更好的做法是，我们内部心里清楚这就是个撒网捞鱼的策略，所以我们才这么搭建的。
text_es: Creo que una mejor manera es que nosotros sabemos internamente que es la red para pescar atún. Por eso la construimos.
original_text: A better way I think is we know internally that it's the tuna fishing net. That's why we built it. That's what it is, but let's just at the beginning, let's put it out there and keep it a little loose and we say, 'It's a net for fish, big fish, all kinds of big fish, any kind of big fish. And then let's just see, let's let the fishermen try it out. Let's see what they pull up.'

vocabulary.definition: Internally refers to activities, processes, or communications that occur within an organization, as opposed to those that involve external parties. It emphasizes the internal workings and dynamics of a company.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, internal communications and processes are vital for ensuring alignment, collaboration, and efficiency among team members and departments.
vocabulary.nuance: This term is often used to distinguish between internal and external perspectives, and it can imply a level of confidentiality or exclusivity regarding the information shared.

vocabulary.definition: Built refers to the process of constructing or creating something, often implying a level of design, engineering, or development. It can pertain to physical structures, software, or systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, the term 'built' is frequently used to describe the development of products or solutions, highlighting the effort and resources invested in their creation.
vocabulary.nuance: This term conveys a sense of accomplishment and intentionality, and it is often used in contexts where the quality or craftsmanship of the creation is emphasized.
